speaker: alice
text: Let's start with the coast, because spring king tides are rolling through south east Queensland right now and local groups are out there doing tide watches and beach clean ups. It's one of those lovely low key community efforts that never really gets a headline but keeps our beaches in good nick.

speaker: charlie
text: Yeah I love that one, no fuss, just neighbours grabbing a bucket and a bit of gumption. Meanwhile up north the reef crew are prepping their gear for coral spawning season, which usually fires up a bit later in the year after the full moon.

speaker: alice
text: It's basically the reef's version of a fireworks show, all those coral polyps releasing at once under the water. Scientists reckon healthy spawning events are a really good sign the reef is bouncing back in patches, which is the kind of good news we like around here.
